transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I don’t enjoy my classes or my art anymore, and the things that used to excite me just feel flat and pointless. I just feel like I'm going through the motions every day without any real joy.
Have you felt this way for most of the past two years, or did this low mood start more recently as a distinct change from your usual self?

No, it hasn't been two years, but it is definitely a distinct change from my usual self. This all started about eight months ago, right after I was passed over for a promotion at work that I had really hoped for.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling this low, where you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, at any point in your life prior to these last eight months?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before. This is the very first time I've felt this low, and it all really started about eight months ago.
Since this started eight months ago, have you noticed any persistent changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or your ability to concentrate?

My sleep has been terrible; I either lie awake replaying work issues or wake up anxious around 3 or 4 AM and can't get back to sleep, leaving me exhausted and foggy. I haven't noticed any significant changes in my appetite, though.

Since these symptoms began, have you found yourself unable to function in your daily life, such as being unable to work or perform basic self-care, or are you still managing to keep up with your responsibilities despite feeling this way?

I'm still going to work, but my ability to function has really suffered—I've fallen behind on grading, canceled student art activities, and started avoiding department events. At home, my husband has had to pick up most of the household tasks because I just don't have the energy or motivation to keep up.
Have you experienced any moments where you felt completely unable to move or speak, or have you had any thoughts that life is no longer worth living?

I haven't experienced being unable to move or speak, but I have had thoughts about life not being worth living. On my worst days, I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up or could quietly slip away. I don't have any plans or intentions to act on those thoughts, though.
Beyond the lack of energy, do you feel that your symptoms are so severe that you are unable to carry out any of your social, work, or domestic activities at all?

No, I'm not completely unable to do anything, but these symptoms have severely disrupted my daily life. I've fallen behind on grading and am avoiding department events and student art activities, while at home my husband has had to take over almost all of the household chores. I just don't have the energy or motivation to keep up with my responsibilities like I used to.

Have you noticed if you feel physically restless and unable to sit still, or conversely, that you feel physically slowed down and heavy, making your movements and speech feel like they are in slow motion?

I haven't really noticed feeling particularly restless or physically slowed down in my movements or speech. I just feel incredibly exhausted and tired all the time, which makes everything feel like a massive effort.
On a typical day, would you say you are still able to carry out some of your essential work and home tasks, or does your low mood and lack of energy leave you almost entirely unable to function?

I am still barely dragging myself through the motions of teaching, but my functioning is severely impacted. I've fallen behind on grading, canceled student art activities, and avoided department events, while my husband has had to take over most of the household chores. I just don't have the energy or motivation to keep up with anything beyond the absolute bare minimum.
